title: WISE: World Knowledge-Informed Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-Image Generation
claim: Prior benchmarks use simple prompts needing only shallow alignment; ours uses prompts demanding world knowledge and reasoning to separate models.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, bottom-up flow, left icon legend, check/cross marks
description: A two-panel comparison with a small icon legend on the far left (Results Comparison, Model Forward, Validation Dimension). Panel (a), on a blue-gray background, is titled 'Previous Straightforward Benchmark'. At the bottom a box lists dimensions: Attribute, Counting, Colors, Object, Position. Arrows labeled 'Sampling' lead up to the prompt 'A photo of two bananas'. Arrows labeled Model A and Model B lead to two near-identical banana photos under the question 'Which one is better?'. Panel (b), on a cream background, is titled 'Our World Knowledge Evaluation'. Its bottom box lists Natural Science, Cultural Common Sense and Spatio-Temporal Reasoning. Sampling leads to the prompt 'Einstein's favorite musical instrument'. Model A produces a violin and gets a green check, labeled 'Reasoning' with a brain-head icon. Model B produces a piano and gets a red cross, labeled 'Failed Reasoning'. The eye goes first to the banana and violin/piano images.
caption: Comparison of previous straightforward benchmarks and our proposed WISE. (a) Previous benchmarks typically use simple prompts, such as "A photo of two bananas" in GenEval [ref], which only require shallow text-image alignment. (b) WISE, in contrast, uses prompts that demand world knowledge and reasoning, such as "Einstein's favorite musical instrument," to evaluate a model's ability to generate images based on deeper understanding.
abstract: Text-to-Image (T2I) models are capable of generating high-quality artistic creations and visual content. However, existing research and evaluation standards predominantly focus on image realism and shallow text-image alignment, lacking a comprehensive assessment of complex semantic understanding and world knowledge integration in text-to-image generation. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{WISE}, the first benchmark specifically designed for \textbf{W}orld Knowledge-\textbf{I}nformed \textbf{S}emantic \textbf{E}valuation. WISE moves beyond simple word-pixel mapping by challenging models with 1000 meticulously crafted prompts across 25 subdomains in cultural common sense, spatio-temporal reasoning, and natural science. To overcome the limitations of traditional CLIP metric, we introduce \textbf{WiScore}, a novel quantitative metric for assessing knowledge-image alignment. Through comprehensive testing of 20 models (10 dedicated T2I models and 10 unified multimodal models) using 1,000 structured prompts spanning 25 subdomains, our findings reveal significant limitations in their ability to effectively integrate and apply world knowledge during image generation, highlighting critical pathways for enhancing knowledge incorporation and application in next-generation T2I models. Code and data are available at \href{https://github.com/PKU-YuanGroup/WISE}{PKU-YuanGroup/WISE}.
